title: PID CPU-steal inspector playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook documents a lightweight investigator for transient 'CPU steal' / scheduling stalls observed in production serving processes. It focuses on fast signals, reproducible capture steps, flamegraph/eBPF traces, and a small CI job pattern to auto-capture artifacts when a perf regression is suspected. Intended for on-call SREs and serving-runtime engineers.

Background / why this matters:
- CPU-steal (steal_time) shows up when the hypervisor or another tenant preempts vCPUs or when cgroup scheduling/misconfig causes long off-CPU periods. For our inference runtime, even short steals during token-generation hot loops cause high tail latency.
- Symptoms: sporadic high p99/p999 latency, CPU usage not saturated but request latencies spike, KV cache misses unrelated.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm symptom window and service PID(s). Grab timeline from traces/otel.
2) top -H -p <pid> to see thread-level states. Look for many 'D' or long wakeups.
3) pidstat -t -p <pid> 1 5 -> look for high %st (steal) or large sleep times per thread.
4) vmstat 1 20 and sar -w show system-wide context switch pressure.
5) dmesg | tail -n 200 for scheduler or cgroup OOM/eviction logs.
6) Check node-level utilization: kubectl top nodes, docker stats or cloud console.
7) If reproducing: scale to single replica and run microbench to make capture easier.

Fast capture commands (non-root friendly notes included):
- Perf stat quick: sudo perf stat -e cpu-clock,cycles,instructions,context-switches,cpu-migrations,cs -p <pid> sleep 10
- Check steal time: cat /proc/stat -> look at the 'steal' field (steal is system-wide), or use: mpstat -P ALL 1 5
- Thread wake info: sudo perf record -F 99 -p <pid> -g -- sleep 15; sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.fold; flamegraph.pl out.fold > perf-flame.svg
- If perf_event_paranoid prevents capture, fallback to bpftrace one-liners (no kernel module needed on many distros): sudo bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:sched:sched_switch /pid == PID/ { @[comm] = hist(delta); }'

eBPF probes to capture off-CPU stacks (low noise):
- offcputime (BCC) collection: sudo /usr/share/bcc/tools/offcputime -p <pid> -f > offcputime.fold; flamegraph.pl offcputime.fold > offcpu-flame.svg
- bpftrace example to get off-CPU histogram per-thread: sudo bpftrace -e '\n  tracepoint:sched:sched_switch /args->prev_pid == PID/ { @off[comm] = hist(nsecs - args->prev_state); }\n'\n(Adapt the predicate for your kernel tracepoint version.)

Annotating flamegraphs with symbols from stripped runtime binaries:
- If runtime builds are stripped in CI, ship a separate symbol archive. Use addr2line or llvm-symbolizer to annotate 'perf script' stacks: perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl --num-entries=100 | ./flamegraph.pl --colors=io > annotated.svg
- For native + Python mixed stacks (our C++ runtime + python harness), enable frame pointers at compile-time and keep a matching build-id store under s3://redwood-symbols/<build-id>/

Example minimal capture script (store under /usr/local/bin/capture-pid-steal.sh):
#!/bin/bash
PID=$1
OUTDIR=/tmp/capture-pid-${PID}-$(date +%s)
mkdir -p $OUTDIR
sudo perf record -F 99 -p $PID -g -- sleep 10 -o $OUTDIR/perf.data || exit 1
sudo perf script -i $OUTDIR/perf.data > $OUTDIR/perf.script
# collapse + flamegraph tools expected in PATH
stackcollapse-perf.pl $OUTDIR/perf.script > $OUTDIR/perf.fold
flamegraph.pl $OUTDIR/perf.fold > $OUTDIR/perf.svg
echo "Artifacts written to $OUTDIR"

CI job pattern (perf-ci-lite) to auto-collect when e2e latency regressed:
- Trigger: nightly benchmark or PR perf guard detects >10% p99 regression.
- Action: spin dedicated tiny node (m5d.xlarge-equivalent), deploy canary runtime with same build-id, run synthetic workload for 30s, run capture script, upload artifacts to S3 and create ticket with links.
- Minimal GitHub Actions snippet (conceptual):
name: perf-ci-lite
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  capture:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - run: ./scripts/run-synthetic.sh --duration 30 --target $SERVICE
      - run: sudo ./tools/capture-pid-steal.sh $CANARY_PID
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: perf-artifacts-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: /tmp/capture-pid-*

Data retention and access patterns:
- Upload raw perf.data and folded stacks to s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/<team>/serving-runtime/<date>/run-id-<id>/
- Keep flamegraphs (SVG) and a short text summary (what we saw, top suspects) as the index file.

Interpretation checklist (what to look for in flamegraph/offcpu):
- One big long horizontal box for a kernel scheduler function or softirq indicates long off-CPU in kernel.
- Many user-space stacks terminating in futex_wait, poll, epoll_wait indicate IO or synchronization stalls (investigate network, storage).
- Off-CPU at the top called 'cpu_idle' or 'xen_steal_clock' suggests hypervisor stealing or noisy neighbor.
- Mixed user+kernel stacks where kernel frames dominate could be preemption due to IRQs or driver issues.
- Measure correlation: cross-reference timestamped flamegraph with tracing spans from zipkin/otlp.

Common root causes we have encountered at Redwood and remediation notes:
- Noisy neighbor on noisy multi-tenant instances (remedy: migrate to dedicated instance type or pin vCPUs with isolcpus and isolate runtime threads, or use Dedicated pools).
- Misconfigured cgroup or low CPU shares for sidecar (remedy: raise cpu.cfs_quota_us or move heavy work into a different cgroup).
- Kernel bug or heavy interrupt storms from NIC (remedy: check interrupt counts, upgrade NIC driver or move to different kernel/hypervisor).
- Frequent context-switch churn from user-level timers (remedy: consolidate timers, use shared timerfd)

Pitfalls & gotchas:
- perf collection overhead: choose sampling frequency carefully (50-200Hz) for production; higher rates add noise.
- perf permission errors: perf_event_paranoid > 1 prevents non-root capture; coordinate with infra or use eBPF probes on host nodes.
- Arm vs x86 differences: tools and symbolization behave differently. Note architecture in artifact metadata.

Follow-up process (after capture):
1) Create ticket with artifact links, short hypothesis, and ask owner of suspected subsystem to comment.
2) If kernel/host causes suspected, escalate to infra with node id, kernel version, and dmesg excerpt.
3) If user-space code suspected, open a runtime issue attaching flamegraphs and a minimal reproducer.
4) If recurring: add a synthetic probe that runs every 5 minutes and uploads a tiny offcpu histogram when p99 > threshold.

Retention and automation roadmap ideas (notes-to-self):
- Build a small service that watches perf-guard alerts and auto-schedules a capture into the Dedicated pool to avoid noisy neighbors during captures.
- Integrate offcputime collector into our existing perf CI with an adaptive sampling budget to cap cost.
- Centralize symbol archive and provide a CLI to fetch symbols by build-id for local annotation.

Appendix: quick command cheat-sheet
- Find top threads by CPU: top -H -p <pid>
- Per-thread stats: pidstat -t -p <pid> 1 5
- Steal time sample: mpstat -P ALL 1 3
- Quick flame: sudo perf record -F 99 -p $PID -g -- sleep 10 && sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.fold && flamegraph.pl out.fold > perf.svg
- eBPF offcpu: sudo /usr/share/bcc/tools/offcputime -p $PID -f | flamegraph.pl > offcpu.svg

Contact / escalation: Evan Martinez (owner), eng-serving-runtime oncall channel #eng-serving-runtime, infra node owners (use node tag from cloud console).

Notes: This is a working draft. Will iterate after two real captures to standardize sampling window and CI thresholds.
